clue.text: Plenty following second test

indicators.note: following says the word for plenty comes after the letter for second

parts.note: plenty means ample, more than enough

explanation.surface: A second exam comes along after plenty of earlier ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A sample is a trial specimen, so to sample something is to test it.

clue.text: Budget for a student place

parts.note: L is the learner plate letter, so a student
to locate is to place or site

explanation.surface: Setting aside money for a student's accommodation.
explanation.definitionFit: To allocate is to set aside funds for a purpose.

clue.text: Rule out comedian's entrance in curtain-raiser

indicators.note: in says that letter is put inside the curtain-raiser word

parts.note: a prelude is an opening piece before the main show

indicators.note: entrance means the first letter of comedian's

explanation.surface: A comic is not allowed to make an appearance in the warm-up act.
explanation.definitionFit: To preclude is to prevent or make impossible in advance.

clue.text: Get rid of ailment that's troubling

indicators.note: troubling means the letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: ie (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: Wanting to be cured of a nagging illness.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate is to remove completely.

clue.text: Standard weapon, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level, as in golf
a lance is a long spear carried by a knight

explanation.surface: A standard-issue weapon, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' looks like a throwaway phrase; 'in' is only a link and the rest is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlance is a particular way of using words, an idiom or jargon.

clue.text: Cause embarrassment when advising how to gain entry to Oxford, for example

definitions.meaning: to blunder tactlessly and cause awkwardness

definitions.text: advising how to gain entry to Oxford, for example
definitions.meaning: an Oxford is a lace-up shoe, so the instruction for getting into one is to insert the foot

explanation.surface: A gaffe made while giving tips on getting into Oxford University.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' looks like the university, but here it is a type of shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make a tactless blunder, and literally describes inserting a foot into a shoe.

clue.text: Oaf receiving no sign of approval as a watchman

indicators.note: receiving says the oaf word takes in the other letters

parts.note: a lout is a boorish oaf
O is nothing, zero, so no
OK signals approval

explanation.surface: A boor gets no thanks for keeping watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A lookout is a sentry posted to keep watch.

clue.text: Pessimistic when vintage harvest is held up by Eurocrats' head

indicators.note: is held up by puts the first piece on top of the letter, as in a down entry
harvest means the letters of vintage are gathered in and reworked
head means the first letter of Eurocrats'

explanation.surface: Wine growers are gloomy when Brussels officials delay the grape harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harvest' signals an anagram of VINTAGE, giving NEGATIV; in a down entry 'is held up by' sets it above E, the head of 'Eurocrats''.
explanation.definitionFit: Negative and pessimistic both describe expecting the worst.

clue.text: It expands developments in general surgery with royal support

indicators.note: support puts the royal letter beneath, at the foot of a down entry
surgery means the word general is operated on and rearranged

parts.note: R is for Rex or Regina, a royal

explanation.surface: Something that enlarges growths in a general surgical ward with royal patronage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developments' are photographic prints, which this machine makes bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: A darkroom enlarger projects negatives to make bigger photographic prints.

clue.text: Shrink from first contact with foreigner

indicators.note: contact with places the piece for first right up against the foreigner

parts.note: an alien is a person from another country
first is written 1ST, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone recoils on first meeting a stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrink' looks like a verb (recoil) but is the slang noun for a psychiatrist; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Alienist is an old word for a psychiatrist, which slang calls a shrink.

clue.text: Asian State long in turmoil

parts.note: MO is the abbreviation for the US state of Missouri

indicators.note: in turmoil means the letters of long are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An Asian country has been in turmoil for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mongol is a native of Mongolia, so a kind of Asian person.

clue.text: Row about keeping single assistant to cook

parts.note: to scull is to row with oars
I, the Roman numeral one, means single
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A kitchen quarrel in which one helper is kept on.
explanation.definitionFit: A scullion was a lowly kitchen servant who did menial jobs for the chef.

clue.text: Tinker with opening to accept foreign currency

indicators.note: to accept says the word for opening takes the currency letters inside it

parts.note: a door is an opening into a room
ct is the abbreviation for cent, a currency foreign to Britain

explanation.surface: Someone fiddles with a slot so that it will take foreign coins.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor something is to tamper with or falsify it.

clue.text: Tell, maybe, of attempt by father to grasp English

indicators.note: to grasp says the word for father holds the English letter

parts.note: dad is an informal word for father
a shot is an attempt, a go

explanation.surface: A tale of a father trying to get hold of the English language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell' looks like a verb, but it is William Tell, the legendary Swiss archer who shot an apple off his son's head.
explanation.definitionFit: William Tell is the classic example of a crack marksman.

clue.text: Perhaps a costumier abroad is on a more appropriate footing?

parts.note: out means away, abroad
fitter means more suitable

explanation.surface: A theatrical dresser working overseas is better placed?
explanation.definitionFit: A costumier supplies clothing, which is what an outfitter does.

clue.text: Apportion blame team incurred to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says only part of the words blame team is taken

explanation.surface: Sharing out responsibility for what the team brought on itself, partly.
explanation.definitionFit: To mete out is to deal out or distribute shares.

clue.text: Sanctions staff appointments

parts.note: to man is to staff
dates are appointments

explanation.surface: Penalties imposed on staff hiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sanctions' looks like penalties but here means authorisations.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandates are official authorisations, as sanctions can be permissions.

clue.text: Spare man on board? It's a matter for conjecture

parts.note: spare means lean, thin
a king is a chessman on the board

explanation.surface: A substitute player on a chessboard is a mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: Conjecture is a form of reasoning, mental work of the mind.

clue.text: Fare reorganisation creating alarm

indicators.note: reorganisation means the letters of fare are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shake-up in ticket prices causes panic among passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: Fear and alarm are both sudden anxiety at danger.

clue.text: Set about right half, say

indicators.note: about says the set word goes round the letter for right

parts.note: a faction is a set or clique

explanation.surface: Getting to work on the right half of a football team.
explanation.definitionFit: A half is one example of a part of a whole number.

clue.text: Flexible headgear for six-footers?

parts.note: six-footers reads as tall people but means insects, whose bendy feelers sprout from their heads

explanation.surface: Bendy hats for very tall people.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects have six legs and a pair of flexible sense organs on the head.

clue.text: His accounts are open to public scrutiny

definitions.text: His accounts are open to public scrutiny

parts.words: His accounts are open to public scrutiny
parts.note: accounts reads as financial books but means news stories, which a journalist publishes for all to read

explanation.surface: A man whose financial books anyone can inspect.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist writes accounts of events that are published for the public.

clue.text: Soldiers joke about direction to get fit again

indicators.note: about places the joke next to the direction letter

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers
E for east is a compass direction
a quip is a witty joke

explanation.surface: Soldiers crack a joke about an order to get into shape again.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-equip is to supply with fresh gear, refitting.

clue.text: Trips conducted initially among Europeans

indicators.note: among says that letter goes inside the word for Europeans

parts.note: Danes, people of Denmark, are Europeans

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of conducted

explanation.surface: Tours led around groups of Europeans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trips' looks like journeys, but as a verb it means dances lightly, as in 'trip the light fantastic'.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip is to step lightly and nimbly, as in a dance.

clue.text: One who gets excited eyeing the birds?

definitions.text: One who gets excited eyeing the birds?

parts.words: One who gets excited eyeing the birds?
parts.note: reads as a man ogling women, but means a keen birdwatcher, one who also jerks nervously

explanation.surface: A man who gets worked up ogling women.
explanation.definitionFit: A keen birdwatcher who chases rare sightings is called this, and it also means someone with a nervous jerk.

clue.text: Lose balance in outing on horseback

parts.note: a trip is an outing or excursion
up means mounted, as a jockey is up on a horse

explanation.surface: A rider falls off during a pony trek.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip up is to stumble and fall over.

clue.text: Biscuit broken about one for nourishment

parts.note: a nut is a small biscuit, as in ginger nut

indicators.note: about says the word for broken goes around the letter for one

parts.note: rent means torn, broken apart
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A biscuit that has crumbled offers some food.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutrient is a substance that provides nourishment.

clue.text: Put one's name to letters giving guidance

parts.note: to sign is to write one's name on
post is mail, letters delivered

explanation.surface: Someone signs letters that contain advice.
explanation.definitionFit: A signpost is an indication pointing the way, so figuratively a piece of direction.

clue.text: Harangued worker in debt

indicators.note: in says the worker goes inside the word for debt

parts.note: in the red means in debt, so red stands for debt
an ant is the classic worker in crosswords, from worker ants

explanation.surface: An employee in debt was given a lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranted means spoke at length in a loud, angry way, lecturing someone.
